# vg-events-api (`vgEventsApi`)

## TL;DR

- `vg-events-api` is a read API for per-call operational data: call lists and details from InfluxDB CDRs, and SIP pcaps from Homer. Its only caller is a linked Cognigy.AI cluster's `vg-resources-api`, never a browser. Design: `vg-resources` `docs/tdd/06-vg-in-ai/025-vg-events-api.md`. The service's README holds the route table and the token contract.
- It is off by default (`vgEventsApi.enabled: false`). Enabling it needs at least one linked AI cluster (`vgInAi.clusters` or `resourceResolver.runtimeApiTargets`) and `homer.enabled`. Without either, the chart fails the render, because the service refuses to start without them.
- With `global.reloadableConfig.enabled` (the default) the link is read live from `cognigy-env-reloadable` and the service starts with no link: it renders unlinked, answers 401 to every request until `AI_CLUSTER_TRUST_LIST` and `VG_CLUSTER_NAME` arrive, and `/health/readiness` stays green (it only checks Redis). This needs the image of vg-events-api PR 17; an older image exits at boot on an empty trust list. The render guard above then does not apply.
- Auth uses the same scheme as feature-server `/v2`: a per-request ES256 JWT from a linked AI cluster, checked against the same `AI_CLUSTER_TRUST_LIST`.
- It is published at `<api host>/events-api/v1/...`. Traefik strips `/events-api`, so the service receives `/v1/...`.

## What renders

| Object | When |
|---|---|
| Deployment and Service `vg-events-api` (HTTP `vgEventsApi.port`, default 4000; probes on `health.port`; metrics on `metrics.port`) | `vgEventsApi.enabled` |
| PodMonitor `prom-cognigy-monitor-cognigy-vg-events-api` | the above and `podMonitors.enabled` |
| Ingress `vg-events-api` and Middlewares `vg-events-api-strip-prefix`, `-body-limit`, `-rate-limit` | the above, at least one target, `ingress.enabled` and `vgEventsApi.ingress.enabled` |
| NetworkPolicy `vg-events-api` (default-deny; see [014-network-policy.md](014-network-policy.md)) | the Deployment, and `vgEventsApi.networkPolicy.enabled` or the FedRAMP profile |
| HPA / ScaledObject `vg-events-api` | `hpa.enabled` (`hpa.services.vgEventsApi.enabled` and its `keda.enabled` default to `true`, so the chart-wide `hpa.enabled` also needs `hpa.keda.enabled`, as for the sibling services) |

The NetworkPolicy's InfluxDB egress matches the in-chart `influxdb` pod only. With an external `influxdb.host`, add its rule to `vgEventsApi.networkPolicy.egressTo`: otherwise every CDR query times out while the pod stays Ready (readiness checks Redis only).

The Ingress chains `ipwhitelistapiserver` (only while the API host's IP allow-list is on: `ingress.api.ipWhiteListMiddleware.enabled`, forced by the FedRAMP profile), then body limit, rate limit, strip prefix — the same allow-list feature-server's `/v2` Ingress reuses.

## Environment

| Env | From |
|---|---|
| `JAMBONES_TIME_SERIES_HOST` / `_PORT` | `influxdb.host` / `influxdb.port`, the same values sbc-inbound, feature-server and api-server use |
| `JAMBONES_TIME_SERIES_RUNTIME_RETENTION_POLICY` | `influxdb.aiRetention.policyName`, rendered only while `influxdb.aiRetention.enabled` (see [Retention of AI-path call data](#retention-of-ai-path-call-data)) |
| `JAMBONES_TIME_SERIES_QUERY_TIMEOUT_MS` | `vgEventsApi.queryTimeoutMs`, rendered only when set |
| `HOMER_BASE_URL`, `HOMER_USERNAME`, `HOMER_PASSWORD` | `homer.urlPrefixServiceConnection` + `homer.serviceName`, `homer.auth.username`, and Secret `vg-homer-password` key `homer-password`, wired as for api-server |
| `HOMER_TIMEOUT_MS` | `vgEventsApi.homerTimeoutMs`, rendered only when set |
| `JAMBONES_REDIS_*` | `redis.*` and `vg.redisAuth.clientEnv`, the same as vg-resource-resolver. Redis is the single-use `jti` store |
| `VG_CLUSTER_NAME`, `AI_CLUSTER_TRUST_LIST` | `vg.aiClusterAuth.env`, the helper feature-server `/v2` uses: `vg.clusterName` and the `jwksUrl` of each effective target (`resourceResolver.runtimeApiTargets` plus those derived from `vgInAi.clusters`) (default `<url without /v1>/.well-known/jwks.json`) |
| `NODE_ENV`, `LOGLEVEL`, `HTTP_PORT`, `HEALTH_CHECK_PORT`, `METRICS_PORT` | `global.nodeEnv`, `vgEventsApi.logLevel` (falls back to `global.logLevel`), `vgEventsApi.port`, `health.port`, `metrics.port` |
| `envFrom: cognigy-env`, `vgEventsApi.extraEnvVars` | as for the other components |

## Ingress

| Ingress | Host | Path | Backend |
|---|---|---|---|
| `api-server` | `ingress.api.host` | `/` (Prefix) | `api-server` |
| `vg-events-api` | `vgEventsApi.ingress.host`, or `ingress.api.host` | `/events-api/` (Prefix) | `vg-events-api:4000` |

api-server already serves `/v1` on the API host, so the service's own `/v1` routes cannot be published unprefixed. Traefik picks the longest matching rule, so `/events-api/...` reaches vg-events-api. The middlewares run in this order:
1. body limit (`vgEventsApi.ingress.maxRequestBodyBytes`, 16 KB; every route is a GET)
2. per-source-IP rate limit (`vgEventsApi.ingress.rateLimit`, 50/s with a burst of 100, the same as `/v2`)
3. `stripPrefix: /events-api`

Entry point and TLS work the same way as for `/v2`. The ingress needs `ingress.ingressClassName: traefik` and a host; the render fails without either.

### `rqh` binds the path after the strip

The JWT's `rqh` claim is `base64url(sha256("<METHOD> <path>[?<sorted query>]"))`, where `path` is **the path the service receives**. That is the path after the strip. The AI-side signer must therefore hash `GET /v1/calls?...`, not the `/events-api/v1/calls?...` URL it actually requests. A signer that hashes the public URL gets `401` on every request (`events_api_auth_rejections_total{reason="request_mismatch"}`).

## Values

```yaml
vgCluster:
  name: vg-prod-eu                   # the JWT `aud`
resourceResolver:
  runtimeApiTargets:                 # the trust list, shared with feature-server /v2
    - name: ai-prod-eu
      url: https://api-eu.cognigy.ai/vg/runtime
homer:
  enabled: true
vgEventsApi:
  enabled: true
  ingress:
    enabled: true                    # host defaults to ingress.api.host
```

`vgEventsApi.image` must stay in `values.yaml`, even while the component is disabled. vg-events-api's preview-release workflow (`helm_values_key: vgEventsApi`) updates that key and refuses to create it.

## Retention of AI-path call data

CDRs and alerts of calls admitted on the AI path carry `organisationId`, `projectId` and `endpointId` tags but no `account_sid`. They are kept on their own InfluxDB retention policy. Everything else is not affected.

| Data | Retention policy | Kept for |
|---|---|---|
| Legacy CDRs/alerts (`account_sid`, or both identities) | the database default, `autogen` | forever, as before |
| AI-path CDRs/alerts on `cdrs` and `alerts` | `influxdb.aiRetention.policyName` (default `vg_ai`), **non-default** | `influxdb.aiRetention.duration` (default `30d`) |

```yaml
influxdb:
  aiRetention:
    enabled: false          # the feature flag; off by default (set true to create the policy)
    policyName: vg_ai       # ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,63}$, not `autogen`
    duration: 30d           # <n>h, <n>d or <n>w, min 1h
    waitTimeoutSeconds: 120 # how long the Job waits for InfluxDB; then warns and exits 0
    hook:                   # the Job's hook settings; keep post-install,pre-upgrade
      hook: post-install,pre-upgrade
      weight: "0"
      deletePolicy: before-hook-creation,hook-succeeded
      backoffLimit: 3
      ttlSecondsAfterFinished: 86400
    resources: {requests: {cpu: 50m, memory: 64Mi}, limits: {cpu: 200m, memory: 128Mi}}
    nodeSelector: {}        # set by the fleet: autoscaler node pool
    tolerations: []
    affinity: {}
```

How it works:
- `@jambonz/time-series` (`runtimeRetentionPolicy`) does the routing: AI-path points are written to, and `queryCdrsByProject` / `queryAlertsByProject` read from, the named policy. The library never creates policies.
- The chart creates them. The hook Job `influxdb-ai-retention` (`post-install,pre-upgrade`, image `jobs.image`) waits for InfluxDB `/ping`, then POSTs InfluxQL to `/query` for each of `cdrs` and `alerts`:
  1. `CREATE DATABASE` (a no-op when the database exists)
  2. `CREATE RETENTION POLICY "<name>" ... DURATION <d> REPLICATION 1` if the policy is missing, otherwise `ALTER RETENTION POLICY ... DURATION <d>`.
- The wait is best-effort. If InfluxDB does not answer `/ping` within `waitTimeoutSeconds`, the Job logs a warning and exits 0, so an InfluxDB outage does not block the upgrade. The policy is then created on the next upgrade, and writers with the runtime-policy fallback (Cognigy/vg-time-series#32) keep writing to the default policy until then. Errors after InfluxDB answers still fail the Job. Keep `waitTimeoutSeconds` plus pod start-up below the release's `helm --timeout` (Helm's default is 5m): Helm's timer starts when it creates the Job, so a wait that outlasts it fails the upgrade with `pre-upgrade hooks failed` before the Job can exit 0.
- The Job is idempotent and runs on every install and upgrade. It never `DROP`s anything and never sets `DEFAULT`. If the policy is somehow a database's default, the Job fails rather than changing `autogen`.
- With the flag on, sbc-inbound, sbc-outbound, feature-server (stable and nightly) and vg-events-api get `JAMBONES_TIME_SERIES_RUNTIME_RETENTION_POLICY=<policyName>`. The render fails on an invalid name or duration.
- Ordering: on an upgrade, the `pre-upgrade` hook completes before Helm applies the workloads that carry the env. A writer therefore never points at a policy that does not exist. On a fresh install, InfluxDB is itself a release resource, so the Job runs `post-install`. A new cluster has no linked AI tenants yet, so no AI-path call is written before the Job finishes.

Changing it:
- **Duration:** set `influxdb.aiRetention.duration` and upgrade. The Job ALTERs the policy, and InfluxDB applies the new duration to existing shards at its next retention check.
- **Name:** a new name creates a new, empty policy. Data in the old policy is not moved or read any more. It expires on the old policy's schedule and the chart does not remove it.
- **Turning it off** (`enabled: false`): no Job and no env. The services write and read everything in the default policy, which is the pre-flag behaviour. The policy and its data stay in place and are not dropped. While the flag is off, the AI side cannot see what was written there (for example in vg-events-api call lists). If the flag is turned back on with the same name, that data becomes readable again, minus whatever has expired. New AI-path data written while the flag was off stays in `autogen` forever.
- It is off by default, so the default render has no Job and no policy env. With the flag on and no InfluxDB (as in kind, `influxdb.replicaCount: 0`), the Job would wait out its timeout before giving up.
